articles.title: England ready to play first Test in Zimbabwe since bad-tempered 1996 tour
articles.summary: ECB commits in principle to match in Victoria Falls. Drawn Test 30 years ago left David Lloyd fuming. England are set to play their first Test match in Zimbabwe since the infamous David Lloyd “we flippin’ murdered ’em!” series in 1996 in the next edition of the International Cricket Council’s…
body: During discussions with Zimbabwe Cricket at the ICC’s quarterly meeting in Bali this week, the England and Wales Cricket Board has committed in principle to visiting for a Test match during the next cycle, although a firm date has yet to be agreed.

The one-off Test would take place at international cricket’s newest venue, the Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium in Victoria Falls, which is due to open next year and will stage four matches at the 50-over World Cup, which Zimbabwe is co-hosting with South Africa.

England’s visit would carry significant symbolic importance as they did not arrange matches against Zimbabwe for more than 20 years in protest at the repressive domestic policies of its government, initially under Robert Mugabe.

In 2008, the ECB announced it was suspending all cricket ties with Zimbabwe and cancelled their scheduled tour of England planned for the following year, five years after England’s players refused to play in a 2003 50-over World Cup group game in Harare due to security concerns.

articles.title: FAA ground stop sends NBA, NHL and college teams scrambling ahead of weekend
articles.summary: Nationwide flight shutdown disrupts team travel in US. Mississippi v Oklahoma football game moved to Sunday. Cavaliers face tight turnaround after Miami travel delay. The Federal Aviation Administration’s decision to ground all flights nationwide for several hours on Friday threw the US sports…
body: Transportation officials cited “extraordinary circumstances” caused by communications issues at regional air traffic control centers for the stoppage. Some teams were left searching for hotel rooms, others rescheduled flights, leagues adjusted start times and several college football programs took the unusual step of chartering buses rather than waiting for the ground stop to end.

“We’re going to allow for general aviation, those larger movements, to take place as a priority. Smaller movements will take lower priority,” the transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said after the ground stop was lifted on Friday night in Washington.

No 19 Mississippi’s football game at Oklahoma was moved from Saturday to Sunday at 1pm ET because of travel issues. Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny criticized the decision, saying the Southeastern Conference had threatened Oklahoma with a forfeit if it did not agree to the change.

“I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances,” Denny said in a statement on X. “Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner nation.”

articles.title: Taylor-Brown wins in Dubai to top T100 standings
articles.summary: British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown moves top of the overall standings in the women's T100 series with her second victory of the season in Dubai.
body: British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings.
The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining.
Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event.
The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series, is aiming for her first T100 world title.

articles.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
articles.summary: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years. There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them.
body: The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7.

“According to our latest evaluation, his brand alone is worth €850m (£710m),” he says. “People identify with his story: a young boy who travelled to Lisbon alone, lost his father and achieved success through his own hard work. Portugal has a long history of great players but no one has ever enjoyed this kind of global exposure. From a marketing standpoint, I have absolutely no doubt that most of the world watched Portugal’s matches because of Cristiano Ronaldo.”

Leonel Pontes, the technical director at Shanghai Shenhua, sees this reality in his everyday life. Pontes played an important role in shaping Ronaldo’s career at Sporting’s academy and became a mentor, helping the teenager from Madeira to cope with homesickness. He later coached Ronaldo as Portugal’s assistant manager and has been in China since 2023.

articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks as Jack Moylan's terrific form for Cardiff City and Republic of Ireland ahead of the Irish's final two Nations League games.

articles.title: NI target challenge of Nations League promotion
articles.summary: A win against Ukraine on Saturday night would leave Northern Ireland needing only a point away to Hungary next week to secure promotion to Nations League A for the first time.
body: Before this Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland had won just one of 16 games played in the second tier of the competition.
But after eight points from four games across September and October, all without conceding a goal, Michael O'Neill's side could end Saturday night as a League A side for the first time.
For that to come to pass, Hungary would need to lose to Georgia in Tbilisi [17:00 GMT] before a Northern Ireland win at home to Ukraine in the later kick-off.

Even if only they hold up their end of the bargain with a win at Windsor Park, the side would travel to Budapest on Tuesday night knowing a point would be good enough to top the group and seal promotion.

articles.title: Goalkeeper Owono given 12-match ban after De Miguel's death from collision
articles.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 matches for his challenge of "excessive force" which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
body: The 25-year-old was sent off after colliding with De Miguel late in the Segunda Division game earlier this month. De Miguel died the following day.
After a review of the incident the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee imposed the maximum punishment on the Equatorial Guinea international.

"The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report, which states that the player was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'," said the committee's statement.

"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances-the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified."

articles.summary: Teenage India sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks the record held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic as the youngest captain in top-level men's Twenty20 cricket.
body: Captaining at the age of 15 years and 232 days, Sooryavanshi broke the record held by Zach Vukusic, who captained Croatia aged 17 years and 311 days.

Bihar lost their opening match in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy - India's domestic state T20 competition, below the Indian Premier League (IPL) - by five wickets to Saurashtra, with Sooryavanshi making 18 from 12 balls.
It is the latest landmark the young career of Sooryavanshi, who became India's youngest men's international in July when he made his T20 debut against England.
He has broken numerous records since making his IPL debut for Rajasthan Royals as a 14-year-old in 2025, becoming the franchise tournament's youngest player.

articles.title: What does a Pochettino team look like?
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been named Manchester United's new manager following the sacking of Michael Carrick, so what can supporters actually expect on the pitch?
body: Mauricio Pochettino takes over from Michael Carrick at Man Utd; former Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea boss brings Premier League experience to the job but what do his previous roles tell us about how his team might shape up at Old Trafford?
The 54-year-old, who led the United States to the last 16 of the World Cup in his most recent role, is returning to England after previous spells in charge of Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea.
Starting with his Southampton tenure, and including his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain head coach, we look at how he has set his team up in each role - and ponder what he might do at United.

A 4-2-3-1 formation quickly became established as Pochettino's favoured choice at Southampton, where he maintained a similar shape to his predecessor Nigel Adkins but with a dramatically different playing style emphasising pressing high up the pitch.

articles.title: WATCH: Boos Ring Out at Rupp Arena During Kentucky’s Game Against Northern Arizona Days After Kansas Loss
articles.summary: Lexington’s Rupp Arena was pretty loud with boos against the home team, the Kentucky Wildcats, despite their narrow one-point victory (78-77) over the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks. This is because Mark Pope’s Kentucky lost to the Kansas Jayhawks in the Champions Classic earlier this week.
body: Despite leading by 13 points in the first half, Kentucky allowed Northern Arizona to fight back, and the road team even took a four-point lead in the final minute. However, after Northern Arizona missed the front end of a one-and-one, Alex Wilkins knocked down the go-ahead three-pointer with two seconds left.

The decisive shot saved Kentucky from a major embarrassment. They were 30-point favorites entering this matchup, and the one-point victory raises more concerns than optimism in Lexington. Wilkins, Milan Momcilovic and Malachi Moreno finished with 14 points each. Moreno also had six rebounds and six assists in the win. On the other hand, Northern Arizona guard Chris Komin was the top scorer with 25 points on 9-for-16 shooting, including 5-of-8 from the 3-point line.
Mark Pope had an interesting response when asked about his message to Lexington fans after a one-point win over Northern Arizona.

Warner has now doubled down on his criticisms of Cricket Australia's probe into the saga, claiming they had not interviewed three of the bowlers - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon - who featured in that Test, as part of what he called a "shoddy investigation".

articles.title: Inter star Francesco Pio Esposito sets incredible record as Italy’s most efficient goalscorer in history
articles.summary: Inter sensation Francesco Pio Esposito has made Italian football history by recording the best goals-per-minute ratio ever seen for the national team. The young striker has surprisingly surpassed Azzurri legends like Luigi Riva and Silvio Piola with his prolific international strike rate.
body: Esposito has officially written his name into the Italian football history books. The 21-year-old has established the best goals-per-minute ratio ever recorded for the Italy national team. The Inter striker has been in sensational form on the international stage, netting nine goals in just 14 appearances for his country. That includes his two goals during the Azzurri’s 3-1 comeback victory over France at the San Siro.

That remarkable return equates to a phenomenal average of one goal every 88 minutes. This astonishing strike rate places the young forward at the very top of Italy's all-time efficiency charts. He has now comfortably outpaced several renowned figures who previously dominated the international scoring rankings.

To put Esposito's remarkable achievement into perspective, his ruthless finishing has seen him eclipse Enrico Chiesa in the record books. Chiesa previously held a highly respected benchmark, averaging a goal every 91 minutes.

However, Chiesa only managed to score seven times during his entire international career with the Azzurri. Esposito has already bypassed that overall tally while maintaining a superior scoring frequency.
